To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feedback-driven control of the number of threads can significantly improve the performance of CMPs.
feedback-driven thread scheduling can improve performance and reduce energy consumption for a variety of workloads on CMP architectures.

1) the run-time behavior (performance and power) of multi-threaded applications on CMPs can be controlled by adjusting the number of threads and 2) the run-time performance and power of an application depends on its input set and machine configuration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem: Given an application with multiple threads, determine the number of threads to execute in order to maximize performance and minimize power.
the following questions: 1) How do we control the number of threads in an application?
developing an automatic feedback-based mechanism for controlling the number of active threads in a multi-threaded application to improve its performance and reduce power consumption on CMPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, the performance and energy-efficiency of CMPs is a function of both the application and the machine configuration, and the number of threads that are executed on a CMP must be determined dynamically.
the number of threads that an application should run with, depends not only on its run-time behavior but also on the machine configuration.
feedback-driven threading improves performance and reduces power for a broad range of multi-threaded applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed and implemented a novel feedback-driven thread scheduling mechanism that adapts to the changing application characteristics and optimizes performance and power for multi-threaded applications.
the performance of an application depends on its run-time characteristics.

the number of threads that maximizes application performance is not fixed and is application, input set and machine dependent and that the run-time behavior can be exploited to determine this optimal number.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the run-time behavior and the performance of a multi-threaded application is a function of its thread-level parallelism (TLP) and the number of threads.
feedback-driven threading is a powerful and effective technique to improve performance and power-efficiency of multi-threaded applications on CMPs.
the number of threads should be dynamically controlled to maximize performance and minimize power consumption.
